core_obligations: Prove (1): use pseudo-coherence to replace K by a bounded complex E of finite projective modules with the same cohomology above m, let n be the largest degree in which E is nonzero, and observe that the case n = m is immediate (proof lines 15977-15985).

For n larger than m, use the vanishing of H^n(E) to see that E^{n-1} to E^n is surjective, split E^{n-1} as E' plus E^n, and replace E by the shorter complex with E' in degree n-1 and zero in degree n, then finish by induction on n (proof lines 15985-15993).

Prove (2) by the same reduction, then identify H^{m+1}(K) with the cokernel of the map E^m to E^{m+1}, which is finitely presented because both modules are finite projective (proof lines 15995-16000).

difficulty_reason: The lemma extracts finiteness statements from pseudo-coherence: if a complex K is m-pseudo-coherent and has no cohomology above m, then the module H^m(K) is of finite type, and if it has no cohomology above m+1 then H^{m+1}(K) is finitely presented (statement lines 15964-15974). The proof is a 24-line argument (proof lines 15977-16000) which uses the defining property of pseudo-coherence to replace K by a bounded complex E of finite projective modules agreeing with K in high degrees, and then argues by descending induction on the top degree n of E: when n = m the top cohomology of E is the cokernel of a map from E^{m-1} into E^m, and when n exceeds m the vanishing of H^n lets one split E^{n-1} as a direct sum of E^n and a smaller module E' and repeat. Part (2) then reads the finitely presented module off as a cokernel of a map between two finite projective modules. The splitting step is where the vanishing of the higher cohomology is really consumed, and the reduction to E is what makes the induction possible.
